statements.statement: Lawsonia inermis (Lythraceae) is the henna plant; its leaves are the botanical source of traditional henna dye material.

limitations: Botanical identity is not a Sujata product specification.
statements.scientificStatement: Lawsonia inermis (Lythraceae) is the henna plant; its leaves are the botanical source of traditional henna dye material.

statements.statement: Lawsone is 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone and is identified as the principal coloring constituent associated with henna leaves.

sourceLocation.paragraph: Lawsone, 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone (I) is the principal active constituent.

statements.scientificStatement: Lawsone is 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone and is identified as the principal coloring constituent associated with henna leaves.

statements.statement: Lawsone content measured in Lawsonia leaf or henna powder is sample- and method-dependent; published examples include about 0.76-0.87 g/100 g dried leaf in one Thai collection and a henna-powder range of 0.004%-0.608% in an earlier HPTLC study.
limitations: These values are not Sujata lot results and cannot be used as a product assay.

marketingInterpretation.example: 헤나 원료의 lawsone 함량은 산지와 분석법에 따라 달라질 수 있다는 점을 설명할 수 있다.

statements.statement: In henna leaves, lawsone is largely present as glycosylated reduced precursors (hennosides); the free dye forms after hydrolysis and oxidation in aqueous medium rather than as a fully developed dye in the intact leaf.

limitations: Explains category chemistry of paste preparation; does not prescribe Sujata usage time.
statements.scientificStatement: In henna leaves, lawsone is largely present as glycosylated reduced precursors (hennosides); the free dye forms after hydrolysis and oxidation in aqueous medium rather than as a fully developed dye in the intact leaf.

marketingInterpretation.example: 건조 잎에서 바로 완성된 염료로 존재하지 않고, 물과 만난 뒤 전구체에서 lawsone이 형성된다는 교육 설명이 가능하다.

statements.statement: Experimental work shows lawsone uptake by keratin fibers is time- and temperature-dependent and consistent with diffusion, with color substantivity increasing after dyeing rather than behaving only as loosely adsorbed surface color.

statements.statement: Permanent oxidative hair dyeing generates colored molecules inside the fiber from small aromatic-amine precursors such as p-phenylenediamine and couplers after peroxide oxidation under alkaline conditions; henna coloring is not this in-fiber oxidative coupling process.

statements.scientificStatement: Permanent oxidative hair dyeing generates colored molecules inside the fiber from small aromatic-amine precursors such as p-phenylenediamine and couplers after peroxide oxidation under alkaline conditions; henna coloring is not this in-fiber oxidative coupling process.

statements.statement: Whole henna leaf material does not behave identically to isolated lawsone on keratin substrates.

statements.scientificStatement: Products sold as henna can contain added p-phenylenediamine; in one European market sample about 36% of tested henna products contained PPD and only about 60% were judged good-quality natural products with at least 0.5% lawsone.

statements.statement: Jojoba seed oil is a liquid wax composed mainly of long-chain wax esters of monounsaturated fatty acids and fatty alcohols, unlike typical triglyceride seed oils.
